sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 v26.04 documentation
sources.evidence: Identifies the exact model, April 28, 2026 release, open weights, Modified MIT license, 256k context and function calling. Its directly fetched .md representation explicitly lists text/image input, reasoning/text output and API names mistral-medium-3-5, mistral-medium-3 and mistral-medium-latest.

sources.title: Official Mistral Medium 3.5 model card
sources.evidence: Describes a dense 128B multimodal model with 256k context, text/image inputs and text output. It supports multilingual use, native function calling and reasoning_effort none/high; distinguishes predecessor Medium 3.1. It flags an earlier Transformers long-context configuration error fixed May 1.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 native checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Specifies 88 language layers, width 12288, MLP width 28672, 96 query heads and 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, vocabulary 131072, untied embeddings and moe=null. Native maximum positions are 262144 with YaRN factor 64; the vision encoder has 48 layers, width 1664 and patch merging.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 Transformers checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Declares Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration with a dense ministral3 language component and Pixtral vision component, matching native dimensions and 262144 maximum positions. FP8 conversion excludes the vision tower, multimodal projector and output head; this revision contains the corrected YaRN configuration.

sources.title: Mistral official model comparison, Medium 3.5 column
sources.evidence: The exact Mistral Medium 3.5 v26.04 column links the same checkpoint and explicitly lists PARAMETERS 128B and ACTIVE 128B. This is a direct nominal active-parameter disclosure, not an inference from dense architecture.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 Modified MIT License
sources.evidence: The checkpoint license is titled Modified MIT License, attributed to Mistral AI in 2026. It includes a restriction when the company or employer exceeded $20 million global consolidated revenue in the preceding month; affected users require other authorization. It is not unrestricted MIT.

sources.title: Mistral Medium legal model lifecycle
sources.evidence: Lists Medium 3.5 as an April 29, 2026 model version, separately from Medium 3.1 on August 12, 2025 and Medium 3.0 on May 7, 2025. Its one-day release discrepancy with inference documentation remains unresolved.

sources.title: Mistral API changelog
sources.evidence: The April 28, 2026 entry explicitly announces release of mistral-medium-3-5, adjustable reasoning and open weights under Modified MIT. This corroborates the inference model page but conflicts with the legal lifecycle day.

sources.title: Remote agents in Vibe, powered by Mistral Medium 3.5
sources.evidence: Current page displays May 22, 2026 and describes remote agents alongside Medium 3.5: dense 128B, 256k context, vision encoder, configurable reasoning and open weights. Its later displayed date cannot replace the earlier documented April release or April public repository activity.

sources.title: Mistral Document QnA architecture
sources.evidence: Explains that document QnA first uses OCR to extract text, structure and formatting, then sends the extracted content to a language model. PDF acceptance is thus a service workflow rather than an additional native checkpoint modality.

sources.title: Official Medium 3.5 repository history
sources.evidence: The current visible main history starts with an April 29, 2026 super-squash at 15:13:01 UTC and includes a same-day merged deployment-documentation pull request. A super-squash does not establish the earliest public release or prove absence of prior availability.

sources.title: Public deployment pull request and Mistral maintainer response
sources.publisher: Hugging Face public event record and Mistral AI maintainer
sources.evidence: Pull request 1 opened April 29, 2026 at 15:23:34 UTC and was merged by Mistral maintainer Julien Denize at 15:43:32 UTC. All 34 public discussion entries were inspected through the public API; none predates April 29. This corroborates public availability by April 29, not April 28.

sources.title: Official FP8 checkpoint tensor index
sources.evidence: Index contains 2465 entries across three Transformers shards, including 1232 activation-scale or weight-scale entries. Storage-element totals and metadata must not be substituted for learned-parameter counts. No full shards or tensor-header census were downloaded.

sources.title: Current Mistral research model overview
sources.evidence: The later current overview separately labels Medium 3.5 as a 128B dense model combining instruction, reasoning and coding, with configurable reasoning and multimodal input. Specifications were not transferred from Medium 3.0, Medium 3.1 or Large models.

name.note: Exact official product name, version 26.04; not Medium 3.0 or 3.1.

developer.note: Catalog display form of Mistral AI, the named model publisher and license attribution.

family.note: Normalized family grouping; the legal table expressly distinguishes its three release generations.

release_date.note: Retain month precision: model documentation and changelog say April 28, whereas the legal lifecycle says April 29. Public repository interaction is confirmed on April 29 but no April 28 interaction was found. The current May 22 blog date and March 31 repository creation are not used as release dates.

open_weights.note: Official checkpoint is publicly accessible with configuration and weight index; open weights does not imply unrestricted licensing.

license.note: Exact checkpoint license title, with a preceding-month company/employer revenue restriction above $20 million; do not normalize to MIT.

parameters_b.note: Mistral-published nominal whole-model count in billions. No exact learned-tensor census is claimed, and FP8 scale entries or byte totals are not counted as model parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: The exact model comparison column independently labels 128B ACTIVE. This nominal developer convention does not establish that the vision encoder runs for every text-only decoding token.

architecture.note: Dense Transformer language decoder with grouped-query attention plus a vision encoder and projector. Native configuration explicitly has moe=null; no expert-routing specification is inferred from a different Medium release.

context_window.note: Supported 256k context agrees with the exact 262144 native and Transformers positional limits. This is model context, not a provider output limit or the Vibe auto-compaction threshold. Earlier faulty YaRN configuration is documented by the card.

modalities.note: Native checkpoint modalities. PDF in the baseline is removed because the linked Document QnA workflow uses OCR preprocessing. Reasoning is text output, not a separate media modality.

reasoning.note: Explicit selectable reasoning_effort none/high, with instruction and reasoning behavior in the same checkpoint.

tool_call.note: Official model page lists function calling, and the exact card supplies native tools/tool_choice examples.

description.value: Mistral model for multilingual chat, reasoning, and tool-assisted workflows
description.note: The baseline description is supported by the exact model card and announcement; no unsupported comparative performance claim is retained.

sources.label: Official comparison with total and active counts
Legal model lifecycle with differing day
Remote agents announcement with later displayed date

patch.notes: 128B total and 128B active are Mistral's nominal model-level disclosures; the active value is explicitly published in its comparison table, not inferred from density or an exact per-token census. The dense multimodal checkpoint accepts text and images; PDF QnA uses separate OCR preprocessing. Native context is 262144 tokens. The Modified MIT license contains a company/employer revenue restriction above $20 million in the preceding month. Release remains April 2026: inference documentation and changelog say April 28, legal lifecycle says April 29, and public repository activity is confirmed April 29. The linked blog currently displays May 22, a later date.

summary: Reviewed all 14 fields for Medium 3.5 v26.04. Correct active parameters from null to Mistral's explicit nominal 128B disclosure and remove PDF from native modalities, retaining its OCR-service explanation. Confirm nominal 128B total, dense multimodal architecture, 262144 context, open weights, exact Modified MIT restrictions, reasoning and function calling. Keep April 2026 month precision because April 28 documentation/changelog and April 29 legal/public-repository evidence do not resolve the day; the current May 22 blog date is later. Only public documentation and repository metadata were fetched, with no complete weights or gated downloads.
